name: Vörðr Warden Tree
body:
VÖRÐR WARDEN TREE
CR 12

This venerable tree towers over the surrounding area at once both intimidating and awe inspiring.

XP 19,200
LN Gargantuan plant
Init +4; Senses blindsight 60 ft., darkvision 60 ft., Perception +20

DEFENSE

AC 31, touch 6, flat-footed 31 (+25 natural, -4 size)
hp 174 (12d8+96)
Fort +23, Ref +12, Will +17
Defensive Abilities guardian roots, thick bark; DR 10/adamantine; SR 25

OFFENSE

Speed 10 ft.
Melee 2 slams +16 (2d10+10/19-20 plus grab)
Space 20 ft.; Reach 20 ft.
Special Attacks sap strength
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 12th; concentration +16)

At will—animal messenger, entangle (DC 15), faerie fire, prayer, status, warp wood (DC 16)
3/day—locate creature, shield other, warp metal (DC 18), wind wall

STATISTICS

Str 30, Dex 10, Con 25, Int 14, Wis 21, Cha 18
Base Atk +9; CMB +23 (+27 grapple); CMD 33
Feats Improved Critical (slam), Improved Initiative, Improved Natural Attack (slam), Power Attack, Toughness, Weapon Focus (slam)
Skills Diplomacy +11, Knowledge (nature) +11, Perception +20, Sense Motive +13, Stealth +11
Languages Common, Elven, Sylvan

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Endless Limbs (Ex)

A warden tree can grapple up to three Medium or smaller creatures without itself gaining the grappled condition and can still make two slam attacks each round while grappling them, or one slam attack when grappling four or more creatures. As a swift action, it can make up to four checks to maintain a grapple on up to four Medium or smaller creatures, making a separate check against each target and dealing its slam damage on a success.

Guardian Roots (Sp)

A warden tree that roots itself in place and does not move for at least 1 hour creates the effects of a guards and wards spell in a 20-foot emanation. Each hour it remains rooted, this emanation increases by 20 feet, up to a maximum of 200 feet. The tree (and a vörðr it manifests as a spirit body) ignores the effects of this guards and wards. If the warden tree moves within the area, the effect remains stationary centered on the tree’s location when it created the effect, but the emanation decreases by 10 feet each minute. If the tree dies or leaves the area, the effect decreases by 10 feet per round.

Sap Strength (Su)

Each round a living creature takes damage from the warden tree’s grapple, its vitality is sapped and it takes 1 Strength damage (DC 23 Fortitude negates). The warden tree heals 10 hit points each time it deals Strength damage. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Spirit Body (Su)

As a full-round action, a warden tree can manifest a vörðr from its own spiritual essence, causing it to take 10 points of damage that cannot be regained until it spends another fullround action touching the vörðr to reabsorb its spirit. This vörðr acts independently from the tree but the tree and vörðr are linked with a telepathic bond. If the tree dies, the vörðr also dies. The vörðr otherwise can exist indefinitely as long as it stays within 1 mile of the warden tree. If it moves farther away, it takes 1 point of damage per round until it dies. If the vörðr dies, the warden tree gains 1 temporary negative level (DC 20 Fortitude negates) for 24 hours and can’t create a new vörðr until the negative level is removed.

Thick Bark (Ex)

A warden tree’s bark is stronger than steel and resistant to magic, granting it a +25 natural armor bonus, spell resistance 25, and a +4 racial bonus on all saving throws (included in the above statistics). If a warden tree fails its save against a blight or horrid wilting spell (or warp wood, which can target the tree as if it were an object) has its bark crack and shrivel, reducing its natural armor bonus and spell resistance by 5 for 24 hours; this stacks with multiple failed saves.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary
Treasure double standard

Vörðr, sometimes called tree-wardens, are spirits which are born to protect a place or person, watching over and defending their charge decisively. They are preeminent guardian spirits and sometimes grow so attached to a place that they become what is known as a warden tree (also known as a værnetræ, tuntre, or vårdträd) so that they may watch their charge as a more unobtrusive, but powerful part of the natural world. In either form, vörðr defend those under their charge from bad luck, offering cryptic advice and mending damage and small hurts as well.

A mature warden tree is a mighty vörðr-spirit rooted into a living tree, ancient grove, sacred orchard, ancestral boundary, or hidden refuge. Unlike lesser guardian spirits that drift unseen through doors and rafters, a warden tree is the ward made flesh: bark harder than worked steel, roots spread like buried walls, and branches strong enough to crush armored intruders.

A warden tree is slow to anger but nearly impossible to ignore once roused. Roads twist beneath its roots, gates refuse to open, thorns rise from the soil, and every path leading deeper into its charge becomes a trap. Those seized by its boughs feel their vigor drawn into the ancient trunk, their strength feeding the guardian that holds them fast.

Most warden trees are not malicious. They are sentinels, oath-keepers, and boundary spirits. A village might honor one as the guardian of its oldest home, a noble line might depend on one to protect a hidden tomb, and a druidic circle might treat one as the living heart of an entire sacred wood.

Creatures living near a vörðr’s tree often leave small offerings or treats to beseech the spirit’s aid in healing a disease or other misfortune. Breaking so much as a twig or plucking a leaf from a vörðr’s tree is considered a serious insult and may bring retribution. Vörðr can be aggressively territorial and do not change their minds easily, but once they decide to bond with a family or community they are dedicated to it. Some families signal their respect for the tree spirit themselves by adopting a family name connected to the type of tree.
